proof.observed: Medians of five runs, p50/p99 ms. From the event's creation: head 457.7/6092.3 against before-591 684.4/17476.1, so head is 1.5 times faster at p50 and 2.9 times faster at p99. From the write's response: head 15.9/674.1 against 26.2/208.3, so head is 1.6 times faster at p50 and 3.2 times SLOWER at p99. Three of the four numbers meet the bar and one misses it; the miss is recorded as an unproven claim below and sent to the architect, since no implementing round can change it. What holds the slow frames back, measured: the event horizon's wait on open transaction ids, not the relay's 2 ms window and not the write. Head logged 'event horizon held back by an open transaction' zero times in all five 0.5x runs where main logged it 1 to 3 times per run; at head the frame tail tracks the longest remaining hold run by run (p99 from the response 674/533/388/690/3542 ms against hold max 748/529/436/1337/1249 ms), and those holders end in 'commit' or in a queued statement of the write batch, database work under this pod's 2 cores. Before-591 predates #2392 and so has no horizon at all: its frames wait on no transaction id although its own writes hold ids 5.7 to 28.1 s, which is why its p99 from the write's response is the one number head does not beat. Measured from the event's creation, which is what a reader waits, head is ahead of before-591 at both percentiles.
proof.negativeControl: The same metric separates the builds the other way at p99 from creation: before-591 17,476.1 ms against head 6,092.3 ms, and main dbdf9318, which has the horizon and not this change, is worst of the three at 1x (frame from creation p99 55,455.0 ms against head's 50,361.1). So the harness measures live-frame latency and is not reporting one build's number for another's.

unproven.claim: Acceptance 2's frame bar misses at one of its four numbers: at half load the live frame measured from the write's own response is 3.2 times slower at p99 than before INFRA-591 (median of five runs, 674.1 ms against 208.3 ms).
unproven.evidence: It is not a defect an implementing round can remove, which is why it is recorded rather than failed. Measured: the head's frame tail tracks the longest open transaction id (p99 from the response 674/533/388/690/3542 ms per run against hold max 748/529/436/1337/1249 ms), those holders end in 'commit' or in a queued batch statement, and the relay's window is 2 ms. Before-591 predates #2392's horizon and waits on no transaction id at all, so no reduction of Dispatch's own holds reaches its number; closing the gap means changing what the horizon waits for, which is dispatch://INFRA-591's design. On the other metric the acceptance names, the frame from the event's creation, which is what a reader waits, head beats before-591 at both percentiles (457.7/6092.3 against 684.4/17476.1). The architect accepted a departure of this shape on 2026-10-29 for the p50 case, with the same cause; this is the same case at p99 and the architect's to rule on. Sent to the architect with these numbers.
